hook: A music app has 500 users. One plan adds 200 users a month; another doubles the users every month. After a year the first plan has 2,900 users and the second has over 2 million. The difference is adding versus multiplying.

prereq.q: What is the common ratio of the geometric sequence $6, 18, 54, \ldots$?
What is the average rate of change of $f$ on $[1, 4]$ if $f(1) = 2$ and $f(4) = 14$?

figure.caption: Over equal steps, $f(x) = 4 + 6x$ adds $6$ each time while $g(x) = 4(1.5)^x$ multiplies by $1.5$. Both start at $4$; the exponential function falls behind at first, then passes the line between $x = 5$ and $x = 6$.

chain.cause: Check that the input intervals have equal length
chain.effect: only then compare the outputs directly

chain.cause: Equal differences over the equal intervals
Equal ratios (not $0$ or $1$) over the equal intervals
chain.effect: an exponential function, $f(x) = ab^x$, or $f(x) = y_1 r^{x - x_1}$ through a known point

ideas: Linear functions extend arithmetic sequences to all real inputs; exponential functions extend geometric sequences.
Linear: over equal-length input intervals, the outputs change by equal amounts. Exponential: over equal-length input intervals, the outputs change by equal factors (they are proportional).
An increasing exponential function eventually passes any increasing linear function.

misconception.wrong: The outputs increase faster and faster, so the function is exponential.
misconception.right: Say both halves with numbers: the input intervals have equal length, and the outputs over them have a constant ratio. Faster and faster growth also fits a quadratic.

summary: Over equal-length input intervals, a linear function adds a constant difference and an exponential function multiplies by a constant ratio. Justify a model type with both halves and the numbers; with unequal steps, compare rates or per-unit ratios instead.
